newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon monitors urge combatants to avoid civilians.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon monitors urge combatants to avoid civilians.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in south Lebanon urged Israeli forces and Hizbollah guerrillas on Wednesday to stay clear of civilian areas in their tit-for-tat war.

The Monitoring Group comprising the United States, France, Lebanon, Syria and Israel said after a three-day meeting that the combatants should also avoid "methods of operation" likely to endanger the civilian population.
The group had discussed three complaints each by Lebanon and Israel over recent alleged breaches of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April.
Both sides accused the other of shelling civilian villages inside or outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.

"The Monitoring Group by unanimity reaffirmed the obligation for all combatants to act strictly in accordance with the Understanding of April 26, 1996, which prohibits attacks on and from civilian populated areas and to avoid using methods of operation which are likely to endanger the civilian population," the monitors said in the statement.

They urged the combatants "to take special precautions around such areas in order to preserve the lives and property of civilians, and called on all those responsible to show restraint to prevent escalation which would put civilians at risk".
The April agreement allows guerrilla raids on Israeli forces in south Lebanon and gives both sides the right to self-defence.
The Group meets at the headquarters of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) in the coastal village of Naqoura in a border zone Israel occupies in south Lebanon.

In Beirut, the foreign ministry said the Group did not condemn or hold any of the two sides responsible for the six incidents due to the interlocking of events and the possibility that they could be interpreted in various ways.
"But the Group was able to agree on practical measures aiming to protect civilians in a better way in future," the ministry added in a statement.

Hizbollah is leading a guerrilla war on some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong allied South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia holding a 15-km (nine-miles) south Lebanon zone set up in 1985 to protect northern Israel from cross-frontier raids.
In the latest incident in south Lebanon, three Israeli soldiers were wounded in a mine explosion inside the occupation zone earlier on Wednesday.
